Atlas historical scene symbols

All scene flags and standards are modern renderings unless identified as photographs of objects. No reconstructed flag is presented as a surviving ancient national flag.
Roman eagle standard and SPQR banner: original Atlas illustrations. Eagle/standards evidence: C. Valerius Flaccus coin, 82 BC, Hamburger Kunsthalle ID235.
Coin photograph: Hamburger Kunsthalle ID235, Martin Ziegert, Public Domain Mark 1.0. https://hamburger-kunsthalle.ikmk.net/object?id=ID235&lang=en
English royal banner SVG: Yaddah / Brunanburh, Wikimedia Commons, public-domain release. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Royal_Banner_of_England.svg
France ancien seme-de-lis: original Atlas rendering of historical royal arms; Pinoteau, La creation des armes de France au XIIe siecle (1982), https://doi.org/10.3406/bsnaf.1982.8766
Ayyubid-period textile photograph: Cleveland Museum of Art 1983.126, Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund, CC0. https://www.clevelandart.org/art/1983.126
Geometric pennant: original decorative Atlas illustration, not an attributed dynastic flag.

Expanded banner gallery:
Las Navas de Tolosa Almohad textile: Las Huelgas, Burgos; Al-Andalus (Met,1992), p.326; photo via Wikimedia Commons Las_Navas_de_Tolosa_banner2.jpg, public-domain reproduction. Catalogue dating 1212–1250, not asserted to be a securely captured 1212 trophy.
Marinid banner of Abu al-Hasan, Fes 1339–1340: Toledo Cathedral; Louvre catalogue Maroc medieval, pp.546–547; image via Wikimedia Commons, public-domain reproduction. Later comparative object.
Abbasid black banner: original plain-colour reconstruction; evidence Gladius 20 (2000), DOI 10.3989/gladius.2000.71.
Hospitaller white-cross banner: original rendering; Order of Malta flags/emblems history (1130 tradition recorded in 1594).
Jerusalem cross banner: original heraldic rendering; motif documented in Met basin 468304, ca.1250–75. No exact c.1200 flag claim.
